summary: The lecture covers Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution, known as the Magna Carta of India, detailing the six Fundamental Rights borrowed from the US Bill of Rights. It explains each right category: Equality (Arts 14-18), Freedom (Arts 19-22), Against Exploitation (Arts 23-24), Religion (Arts 25-28), Cultural/Educational (Arts 29-30), and Constitutional Remedies (Art 32). It notes the removal of Right to Property (44th Amendment, 1978) and emergency provisions affecting Arts 19, 20, 21.
points: Part III (Articles 12-35) called Magna Carta of India; Fundamental Rights borrowed from US Bill of Rights via Nehru's Objective Resolution.
Originally 7 Fundamental Rights; Right to Property (Art 31) removed by 44th Amendment 1978, now legal right under Art 300A.

Article 14-18: Right to Equality - Art 14 (equality before law), Art 15 (no discrimination), Art 16 (equal opportunity in public employment), Art 17 (abolish untouchability), Art 18 (abolish titles except military/academic).

Article 19-22: Right to Freedom - Art 19 (six freedoms), Art 20 (protection against conviction), Art 21 (life/liberty), Art 21A (education, 86th Amendment 2002), Art 22 (protection against arrest/detention).
Article 23-24: Right against Exploitation - Art 23 prohibits forced labour/human trafficking; Art 24 prohibits child labour in hazardous industries.
Article 25-28: Freedom of Religion - Art 25 (conscience/religion), Art 26 (manage religious affairs), Art 27 (no tax for religion), Art 28 (no religious instruction in state-funded institutions).
Article 29-30: Cultural/Educational Rights for minorities - Art 29 (protect language/script/culture), Art 30 (establish/administer educational institutions).
Article 32: Right to Constitutional Remedies (Heart and Soul per Dr. Ambedkar); Supreme Court/High Courts issue 5 writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo Warranto.
During National Emergency (Art 352), Art 19 freedoms automatically suspended; Arts 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during emergency.
Fundamental Rights not absolute; reasonable restrictions permissible for national security, public order, etc.

check.q: Which Amendment removed Right to Property from Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right under Article 300A?
Which two Fundamental Rights cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency under Article 352?
Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court and High Courts to issue five types of writs. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
